history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row (seq 2432, 'Kasar Devi Temple | Almora | Uttarakhand') is the SAME temple already documented as seq 1130 (id kasar-devi-temple-kasar-devi) - the famous Kasar Devi Temple on the Kaashay Hills ~8 km from Almora town on the Binsar Road. No separate shrine named 'Kasar Devi Temple' in Almora town exists; this row duplicates the earlier record and should be merged or dropped. For the temple itself: dedicated to Goddess Kasar Devi; tradition from the Skanda Purana and Devi Bhagavata says goddess Kaushiki defeated the demons Shumbh and Nishumbh here. In 1890 Swami Vivekananda meditated here; in the 1960s-70s it became a hippie-movement focal point (Allen Ginsberg, Timothy Leary, Bob Dylan at nearby Crank's Ridge). Popular sources repeat a 'Van Allen Belt' geomagnetic-zone claim alongside Machu Picchu and Stonehenge without scientific consensus. The complex holds two groups of shrines (Devi; Shiva-Bhairav) with an Akhand Jyoti burning around the clock.

name: Kasar Devi Temple
town: Kasar Devi, Almora district (CSV town 'Almora' is imprecise - the temple is ~8 km from Almora town on the Binsar Road)
town_description: Kasar Devi is a small ridge village on the pine-covered Kaashay Hills at ~2,116 m, about 8 km from Almora. Named for its temple, it is famed for 360-degree views of the Nanda Devi and Trishul ranges, the Crank's Ridge hippie-era settlement, and its calm atmosphere that has drawn meditators and artists for over a century.

travel.airport: Pantnagar Airport (~124 km per travel guide); road onward via Almora
travel.railway: Kathgodam railway station (~88 km per one guide; ~83 km per another - verify), then road to Almora and on to Kasar Devi
travel.road: 8 km from Almora town on the Binsar Road by taxi or local bus; the final approach is a steep ~500 m climb of 100-150 stone steps

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to December; the Kasar Fair at Kartik Purnima (Oct-Nov) draws the largest crowds
